examples: Open warez and spot the three themes by their black mark and palette miniature, the mods by red and the skills by purple.
Press ? in the title strip to see the shipped keys: / search, j k move, enter open, i t u act.
how_to: Open Warez from the menu (hotkey r), or go to /#warez.
Read the mark before each title to know the kind at a glance: mods are red, skills purple, themes black, each with its own glyph, and the card's top edge wears the same color.

Use the left menu: find in warez, then store (everything, newest, updates, one line per kind with its count) and installed (one line per kind, each opening to its installed items with a state word). A needs a look group shows only when something does. Sort, the grid or list choice and search stay in the top row and are remembered on this device.

Choose an installed item to manage it on the right with the same panels as the plugins, themes, skills and mods pages; a plugin's tabs sit on its page. On a phone the menu is the first screen and each choice opens under a back bar.
Open a card to read who signed it first (signer, pinned key, scripts, source, digest), then the description and the context cost; theme cards show the theme's own palette and named swatches.
Add an item from its card, or open it to install to another scope, update or remove it; refresh the index, publish a skill, sign in and the key list (the ? button) sit in the title strip.

If you published an item, open its card to find a card image row: choose a png, jpeg or webp (at least 1200x500, 3:2 to 3:1, up to 512 KiB), see it on the card here only, then send it for review; other people see it after review.
name: Warez
summary: the signed catalog as a faceted shelf: labelled kind, state and sort groups, theme miniatures from each theme's real palette, trust first in the reading pane, and a colored mark before every title (mods red, skills purple, themes black), and a publisher can preview and send their own card image
where: Menu tab, Warez (hotkey r), under Themes.
Also at /#warez, /#catalog, /#warez/<handle>/<name> to open one item, and /#warez/store/... or /#warez/installed/... for a menu node.
